previous.description: Command-line companion for Kronikol. Includes `kronikol merge`, which combines several mergeable TestRunReport.json files (produced with GenerateMergeableData enabled — e.g. by parallel CI runners) into a single combined TestRunReport.html plus the merged TestRunReport.json beside it, so a sharded run is queryable and can serve as a baseline; `kronikol ingest`, which replays language-neutral NDJSON interaction captures (from an out-of-process proxy tap or any non-.NET capturer) into a full Kronikol report; `kronikol query`, which answers questions about a TestRunReport.json — why a test failed, what a service returned, where a wrong value came from — without loading the file, so a 10 MB report is debuggable by tooling and by AI agents; `kronikol export`, which pushes NDJSON interaction captures to an OTLP/HTTP collector as OpenTelemetry spans so the traffic only Kronikol saw appears in Tempo/Jaeger next to the app's real traces; `kronikol ctrf`, which converts a TestRunReport.json into a Common Test Report Format document so CI tooling that already speaks CTRF can read a Kronikol run; and `kronikol init-agents`, which installs the test-debugging skill and the CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md instruction block into an existing repository, so its agents know the report is there and how to read it.

previous.description:
Local-first .NET global tool that checks a stack/config contract before runtime.

stackcontract reads your Docker Compose file and a stackcontract.yml contract, then reports missing services and environment keys. It does not start containers and does not need a Docker daemon for `validate`. Local .env files are inspected for key presence only — values never appear in text or JSON output.

Commands: `stackcontract init` writes a contract from compose (and optional Options assemblies); `stackcontract validate [--strict]` checks the live tree; `stackcontract version` prints the tool version. Exit codes: 0 ok/warnings, 1 any error, 2 usage/parse. Finding codes include SVC_MISSING, ENV_REQUIRED_MISSING, ENV_OPTIONAL_MISSING, ENV_EXAMPLE_UNKNOWN, COMPOSE_PARSE, CONTRACT_INVALID, PROFILE_UNKNOWN.

Legacy ComposeContract names still work: composecontract.yml is accepted when stackcontract.yml is absent. MIT licensed. Not affiliated with Docker, Inc.

Install: `dotnet tool install -g stackcontract`. Pair with StackContract.AspNetCore to fail host start when required configuration keys are missing.

current.description:
Local-first .NET global tool that checks a stack/config contract before runtime.

stackcontract validates Docker Compose and/or appsettings against a stackcontract.yml contract, then reports missing services, env keys, and configuration paths. It does not start containers and does not need a Docker daemon for `validate`. Local .env and appsettings are inspected for key/path presence only — values never appear in text or JSON output. Compose is optional for plain C# / ASP.NET apps.

Commands: `stackcontract init` writes a contract from compose and/or appsettings (and optional Options assemblies); `stackcontract validate [--strict] [--environment NAME]` checks the live tree; `stackcontract version` prints the tool version. Exit codes: 0 ok/warnings, 1 any error, 2 usage/parse. Finding codes include SVC_MISSING, ENV_*, CONFIG_PATH_MISSING, CONFIG_PARSE, COMPOSE_PARSE, CONTRACT_INVALID, PROFILE_UNKNOWN.

Legacy ComposeContract names still work: composecontract.yml is accepted when stackcontract.yml is absent. MIT licensed. Not affiliated with Docker, Inc.

Install: `dotnet tool install -g stackcontract`. Pair with StackContract.AspNetCore to fail host start when required configuration keys are missing.
